alice: quick q — if a request hits a per-route quota but the global pool still has headroom, what should we return to clients? 429 with per-route headers only, or include global hints too? :thinking:
ben: prefer signalling the most specific bucket that caused the rejection. return 429 + per-route headers so SDKs can fallback to route-level backoff. global header can still be present but client should use per-route first.
carla: fwiw some older SDKs only inspect `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`X-RateLimit-Limit`. can we add a stable shim header so older clients can still see which bucket fired? example i'd propose: `X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:abc123`
carla: sample response we'd emit:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:abc123
X-RateLimit-Retry-After: 12
```
ben: sounds good. also add `X-RateLimit-Scopes: route=abc123` for our routing/telemetry tools to parse. semantics: if both per-route and global limits are hit, include both sets of headers (route-specific + global) but clients pick route-specific for backoff.
alice: ok can we make that explicit in the contract doc and call out the precedence? i can update the spec and add a tiny migration note for SDKs.
ben: i'll add a runtime shim so older backends emit `X-RateLimit-Bucket` automatically when a route quota triggers. will include unit tests for header precedence + an integration Canary.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for feature/rl-route-shim at 3412345760 :rocket:
carla: leaving a TODO — run canary in eu-west1 and us-west2 for 30m to watch soft-429 rates after the shim flips on. also check our per-route metrics pipeline hasn't regressed.
alice: perfect, thanks both :thumbsup:
